findings.source_quote: “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the quoted sentence with a Swedish translation that preserves the printed meaning, for example: “Gråt kan vara natten lång, men jubel kommer om morgonen” (Psaltaren 30:5).
findings.translation_quote: “Gråt kan vara en natt, men jubel kommer om morgonen” (Psaltaren 30:5).

findings.source_quote: “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion” (Psalm 71:1).
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the printed assertion of trust rather than substituting the different image of taking refuge; for example: “Till dig, HERRE, sätter jag min tillit; låt mig aldrig komma på skam” (Psaltaren 71:1).
findings.translation_quote: “Till dig, HERRE, tar jag min tillflykt; låt mig aldrig komma på skam” (Psaltaren 71:1).

findings.location: Article body, paragraph beginning “Sometimes this type of overload…”
findings.source_quote: “Traumatic events in our plain circles tend to receive prayer, finances, and weekly budget updates.”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the unclear English-derived phrase “plain-gemenskaper” with a clear Swedish equivalent for the communities meant, for example “våra konservativa kristna gemenskaper,” if that matches the publication’s usage.
findings.translation_quote: “Traumatiska händelser i våra plain-gemenskaper får ofta förbön, ekonomiskt stöd och veckovisa uppdateringar om budgeten.”
